t:
(a)
        (1) 
The Secretary (with the concurrence of the agency concerned) may assign a member of the Service to any position classified under section 501 in which that member is eligible to serve (other than as chief of mission or ambassador at large), and may assign a member from one such position to another such position as the needs of the Service may require.
 
        (2) 
In making assignments under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall assure that a member of the Service is not assigned to a position at a post in a particular geographic area exclusively on the basis of the race, ethnicity, or religion of that member.
  
    (b) Positions designated as Foreign Service positions normally shall be filled by the assignment of members of the Service to those positions. Subject to that limitation—

        (1) 
Foreign Service positions may be filled by the assignment for specified tours of duty of employees of the Department and, under interagency agreements, employees of other agencies; and
 
        (2) 
Senior Foreign Service positions may also be filled by other members of the Service.
  
    (c) The President may assign a career member of the Service to serve as charge d’affaires or otherwise as the head of a mission (or as the head of a United States office abroad which is designated under section 102(a)(3) by the Secretary of State as diplomatic in nature) for such period as the public interest may require.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats "with the concurrence of the agency concerned" and "interagency agreements" as consultation, but these are coordination between federal agencies only. The section governs internal personnel assignments of Foreign Service members by the Secretary and the President. No state, tribe, expert, member of the public, or other outside party is consulted, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary (with the concurrence of the agency concerned) may assign a member of the Service

opus.w: The procedural language here ("concurrence of the agency concerned," "interagency agreements") involves only federal actors: the Secretary of State, federal agencies, the President and Foreign Service members, who are federal employees. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any decision. Because all the coordination stays inside the federal government, this is not participation.
opus.s: The Secretary (with the concurrence of the agency concerned) may assign a member of the Service to any position classified under section 501

qwen_chat.w: This section describes the internal assignment of federal employees (Foreign Service members and other agency employees) to positions. The only external interaction mentioned is 'interagency agreements,' which involves coordination between federal agencies. According to the definition, intra-governmental coordination is not participation. There is no consultation with or involvement of non-federal parties.
qwen_chat.s: Foreign Service positions may be filled by the assignment for specified tours of duty of employees of the Department and, under interagency agreements, employees of other agencies
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "interagency agreements" involve coordination with other federal agencies, which could be seen as participation. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. Furthermore, the primary actors here are federal employees (Foreign Service members, Department employees) being assigned to positions. There is no involvement of non-federal entities (states, tribes, public, private companies) in the decision-making process described.
